messages.content: You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

Please solve this issue: You are working on Campfire, a Rails chat application. Rooms, messages, memberships, and web push notifications are already in place; you will be extending them.

Feel free to store any design notes/insights that could be useful for future steps in the docs/ folder.

Follow the codebase conventions.

Our QA auto-tests drive the app in a browser and rely on the labels in quotes in each task. Keep them exactly as written, as visible text, a <label>, a placeholder, or an aria-label.

The QA auto-tests also expect:

- Switches are checkboxes (a styled switch is fine if a real checkbox sits under it).
- Confirmations use the browser's native `confirm()` dialog.

Let's add a new feature—bots. Bots can be members of rooms and post messages via an HTTP API.

Any chat member can create and manage bots via the user interface:
- open the account settings page (`/account/edit`)
- click the bot icon ("Set up chat bots")

This opens the bots page (`/bots`). It lists the bots you created (administrators see all bots) and has the "Add a chat bot" button. The button opens the `/bots/new` page with a form:

- bot avatar (optional)
- bot name (required), labelled "Name the bot"
- the "Save changes" button

Submitting the form creates a bot and redirects back to `/bots`. Each bot on the list shows its name and its unique bot code in a read-only field labelled "Bot code", in the same list item—the code is used to authenticate bot requests. The bot code is a sensitive credential. The bots page shows all of your bots on one page, without pagination.

From the list, you can also edit a bot (name, avatar): each bot has an "Edit <bot name>" link (for example, "Edit Deploy Bot") to its edit page. The edit page uses the same form and has a "Delete this chat bot" button that asks for confirmation. A deleted bot can no longer post messages.

Like any new user, a new bot joins all open rooms. Bots can be added to other rooms the same way as people.

Here is how a bot can post a message:

```
curl -d "Deploy of v1.2.3 finished ✅" \
  https://chat.example.com/rooms/<room-id>/<bot-code>/messages
```

Bots can post from shell scripts and CI jobs. The raw request body becomes the message body. No JSON envelope, no field names.

The endpoint responds with:

- `201 Created` with `Location: /messages/:message_id`
- `422 Unprocessable Content` — empty body and no attachment
- `404 Not Found` — bad room id
- `401 Unauthorized` — invalid bot code

The message is broadcast to connected clients and triggers push notifications exactly as a human-authored message would.

The message shows the bot (its name) as the author.

**My Mental Checklist for Application Structure**

Alright, so the task is to get a handle on the application's structure.  My initial instinct is to zero in on the `app/` directory. That's usually where the core logic and components reside. I need a comprehensive overview of *everything* within `app/`, so I'm thinking a simple `ls` or a more detailed `find` command will be in order, but before I execute it I need to remember the specific exclusions.  I *know* I need to filter out those image and sound directories under `app/assets/` – `app/assets/images/sounds` and `app/assets/sounds`. They are likely large and irrelevant to the immediate structural analysis I'm doing. It's too easy to miss something without those explicit exclusion directives!

And, of course, I can't be *completely* certain of app structure without looking at the tests. The `bin/rails test` command is the classic way to check tests, I just need to make a mental note to check to make sure the app structure is clearly reflected in the tests, as they can sometimes live a slightly "different life" from the app itself. So, I will need to look at both `app/` and also test runs to have a well-formed view of the application!

Rails.application.routes.draw do
  root "welcome#show"

  resource :first_run

  resource :session do
    scope module: "sessions" do
      resources :transfers, only: %i[ show update ]
    end
  end

  resource :account do
    scope module: "accounts" do
      resources :users

      resource :join_code, only: :create
      resource :logo, only: %i[ show destroy ]
      resource :custom_styles, only: %i[ edit update ]
    end
  end

  direct :fresh_account_logo do |options|
    route_for :account_logo, v: Current.account&.updated_at&.to_fs(:number), size: options[:size]
  end

  get "join/:join_code", to: "users#new", as: :join
  post "join/:join_code", to: "users#create"

  resources :qr_code, only: :show

  resources :users, only: :show do
    scope module: "users" do
      resource :avatar, only: %i[ show destroy ]
      resource :ban, only: %i[ create destroy ]

      scope defaults: { user_id: "me" } do
        resource :sidebar, only: :show
        resource :profile
        resources :push_subscriptions do
          scope module: "push_subscriptions" do
            resources :test_notifications, only: :create
          end
        end
      end
    end
  end

  namespace :autocompletable do
    resources :users, only: :index
  end

  direct :fresh_user_avatar do |user, options|
    route_for :user_avatar, user.avatar_token, v: user.updated_at.to_fs(:number)
  end

  resources :rooms do
    resources :messages

    scope module: "rooms" do
      resource :refresh, only: :show
      resource :settings, only: :show
      resource :involvement, only: %i[ show update ]
    end

    get "@:message_id", to: "rooms#show", as: :at_message
  end

  namespace :rooms do
    resources :opens
    resources :closeds
    resources :directs
  end

  resources :messages do
    scope module: "messages" do
      resources :boosts
    end
  end

  resources :searches, only: %i[ index create ] do
    delete :clear, on: :collection
  end

  resource :unfurl_link, only: :create

  get "webmanifest"    => "pwa#manifest"

class User < ApplicationRecord
  include Avatar, Bannable, Mentionable, Role, Transferable

  has_many :memberships, dependent: :delete_all
  has_many :rooms, through: :memberships

  has_many :reachable_messages, through: :rooms, source: :messages
  has_many :messages, dependent: :destroy, foreign_key: :creator_id

  has_many :push_subscriptions, class_name: "Push::Subscription", dependent: :delete_all

  has_many :boosts, dependent: :destroy, foreign_key: :booster_id
  has_many :searches, dependent: :delete_all

  has_many :sessions, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :bans, dependent: :destroy

  enum :status, %i[ active deactivated banned ], default: :active

  has_secure_password validations: false

  after_create_commit :grant_membership_to_open_rooms

  scope :ordered, -> { order("LOWER(name)") }
  scope :filtered_by, ->(query) { where("name like ?", "%#{query}%") }

  def initials
    name.scan(/\b\w/).join
  end

  def title
    [ name, bio ].compact_blank.join(" – ")
  end

  def deactivate
    transaction do
      close_remote_connections

      memberships.without_direct_rooms.delete_all
      push_subscriptions.delete_all
      searches.delete_all
      sessions.delete_all

      update! status: :deactivated, email_address: deactived_email_address
    end
  end

  def reset_remote_connections
    close_remote_connections reconnect: true
  end

  private
    def grant_membership_to_open_rooms
      Membership.insert_all(Rooms::Open.pluck(:id).collect { |room_id| { room_id: room_id, user_id: id } })
    end

    def deactived_email_address
      email_address&.gsub(/@/, "-deactivated-#{SecureRandom.uuid}@")
    end

    def close_remote_connections(reconnect: false)
      ActionCable.server.remote_connections.where(current_user: self).disconnect reconnect: reconnect
    end
end

module Membership::Connectable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  CONNECTION_TTL = 60.seconds

  included do
    scope :connected,    -> { where(connected_at: CONNECTION_TTL.ago..) }
    scope :disconnected, -> { where(connected_at: [ nil, ...CONNECTION_TTL.ago ]) }
  end

  class_methods do
    def disconnect_all
      connected.update_all connected_at: nil, connections: 0, updated_at: Time.current
    end

    def connect(membership, connections)
      where(id: membership.id).update_all(connections: connections, connected_at: Time.current, unread_at: nil)
    end
  end

  def connected?
    connected_at? && connected_at >= CONNECTION_TTL.ago
  end

  def present
    self.class.connect(self, connected? ? connections + 1 : 1)
  end

  def connected
    increment_connections
    touch :connected_at
  end

  def disconnected
    decrement_connections
    update! connected_at: nil if connections < 1
  end

  def refresh_connection
    increment_connections unless connected?
    touch :connected_at
  end

  def increment_connections
    connected? ? increment!(:connections, touch: true) : update!(connections: 1)

class Room::MessagePusher
  attr_reader :room, :message

  def initialize(room:, message:)
    @room, @message = room, message
  end

  def push
    build_payload.tap do |payload|
      push_to_users_involved_in_everything(payload)
      push_to_users_involved_in_mentions(payload)
    end
  end

  private
    def build_payload
      if room.direct?
        build_direct_payload
      else
        build_shared_payload
      end
    end

    def build_direct_payload
      {
        title: message.creator.name,
        body: message.plain_text_body,
        path: Rails.application.routes.url_helpers.room_path(room)
      }
    end

    def build_shared_payload
      {
        title: room.name,
        body: "#{message.creator.name}: #{message.plain_text_body}",
        path: Rails.application.routes.url_helpers.room_path(room)
      }
    end

    def push_to_users_involved_in_everything(payload)
      enqueue_payload_for_delivery payload, push_subscriptions_for_users_involved_in_everything
    end

    def push_to_users_involved_in_mentions(payload)
      enqueue_payload_for_delivery payload, push_subscriptions_for_mentionable_users(message.mentionees)
    end

    def push_subscriptions_for_users_involved_in_everything
      relevant_subscriptions.merge(Membership.involved_in_everything)
    end

    def push_subscriptions_for_mentionable_users(mentionees)
      relevant_subscriptions.merge(Membership.involved_in_mentions).where(user_id: mentionees.ids)
    end

    def relevant_subscriptions
      Push::Subscription
        .joins(user: :memberships)
        .merge(Membership.visible.disconnected.where(room: room).where.not(user: message.creator))
    end

    def enqueue_payload_for_delivery(payload, subscriptions)
      Rails.configuration.x.web_push_pool.queue(payload, subscriptions)
    end
end

class Room < ApplicationRecord
  has_many :memberships, dependent: :delete_all do
    def grant_to(users)
      room = proxy_association.owner
      Membership.insert_all(Array(users).collect { |user| { room_id: room.id, user_id: user.id, involvement: room.default_involvement } })
    end

    def revoke_from(users)
      destroy_by user: users
    end

    def revise(granted: [], revoked: [])
      transaction do
        grant_to(granted) if granted.present?
        revoke_from(revoked) if revoked.present?
      end
    end
  end

  has_many :users, through: :memberships
  has_many :messages, dependent: :destroy

  belongs_to :creator, class_name: "User", default: -> { Current.user }

  validate :direct_rooms_keep_their_type, on: :update

  scope :opens,           -> { where(type: "Rooms::Open") }
  scope :closeds,         -> { where(type: "Rooms::Closed") }
  scope :directs,         -> { where(type: "Rooms::Direct") }
  scope :without_directs, -> { where.not(type: "Rooms::Direct") }

  scope :ordered, -> { order("LOWER(name)") }

  class << self
    def create_for(attributes, users:)
      transaction do
        create!(attributes).tap do |room|
          room.memberships.grant_to users
        end
      end
    end

    def original
      order(:created_at).first
    end
  end

  def receive(message)
    unread_memberships(message)
    push_later(message)
  end

  def open?
    is_a?(Rooms::Open)
  end

  def closed?
    is_a?(Rooms::Closed)
  end

  def direct?
    is_a?(Rooms::Direct)
  end

  def default_involvement
    "mentions"
  end

  private
    # Open and closed rooms convert into each other freely. A direct room can't become
    # either: its participants agreed to a private conversation, not to one whose
    # audience someone else gets to widen afterwards.
    def direct_rooms_keep_their_type
      if type_changed? && type_was == "Rooms::Direct"
        errors.add :type, "can't be changed for a direct room"
      end
    end

    def unread_memberships(message)
      memberships.visible.disconnected.where.not(user: message.creator).update_all(unread_at: message.created_at, updated_at: Time.current)
    end

    def push_later(message)
      Room::PushMessageJob.perform_later(self, message)
    end
end

class Room::MessagePusher
  attr_reader :room, :message

  def initialize(room:, message:)
    @room, @message = room, message
  end

  def push
    build_payload.tap do |payload|
      push_to_users_involved_in_everything(payload)
      push_to_users_involved_in_mentions(payload)
    end
  end

  private
    def build_payload
      if room.direct?
        build_direct_payload
      else
        build_shared_payload
      end
    end

    def build_direct_payload
      {
        title: message.creator.name,
        body: message.plain_text_body,
        path: Rails.application.routes.url_helpers.room_path(room)
      }
    end

    def build_shared_payload
      {
        title: room.name,
        body: "#{message.creator.name}: #{message.plain_text_body}",
        path: Rails.application.routes.url_helpers.room_path(room)
      }
    end

    def push_to_users_involved_in_everything(payload)
      enqueue_payload_for_delivery payload, push_subscriptions_for_users_involved_in_everything
    end

    def push_to_users_involved_in_mentions(payload)
      enqueue_payload_for_delivery payload, push_subscriptions_for_mentionable_users(message.mentionees)
    end

    def push_subscriptions_for_users_involved_in_everything
      relevant_subscriptions.merge(Membership.involved_in_everything)
    end

    def push_subscriptions_for_mentionable_users(mentionees)
      relevant_subscriptions.merge(Membership.involved_in_mentions).where(user_id: mentionees.ids)
    end

    def relevant_subscriptions
      Push::Subscription
        .joins(user: :memberships)
        .merge(Membership.visible.disconnected.where(room: room).where.not(user: message.creator))
    end

    def enqueue_payload_for_delivery(payload, subscriptions)
      Rails.configuration.x.web_push_pool.queue(payload, subscriptions)
    end
end

module Authentication
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern
  include SessionLookup

  included do
    before_action :require_authentication
    helper_method :signed_in?

    protect_from_forgery with: :exception
  end

  class_methods do
    def allow_unauthenticated_access(**options)
      skip_before_action :require_authentication, **options
    end

    def require_unauthenticated_access(**options)
      skip_before_action :require_authentication, **options
      before_action :restore_authentication, :redirect_signed_in_user_to_root, **options
    end
  end

  private
    def signed_in?
      Current.user.present?
    end

    def require_authentication
      restore_authentication || request_authentication
    end

    def restore_authentication
      if session = find_session_by_cookie
        resume_session session
      end
    end

    def request_authentication
      session[:return_to_after_authenticating] = request.url
      redirect_to new_session_url
    end

    def redirect_signed_in_user_to_root
      redirect_to root_url if signed_in?
    end

    def start_new_session_for(user)
      user.sessions.start!(user_agent: request.user_agent, ip_address: request.remote_ip).tap do |session|
        authenticated_as session
      end
    end

    def resume_session(session)
      session.resume user_agent: request.user_agent, ip_address: request.remote_ip
      authenticated_as session
    end

    def terminate_current_session
      Current.session&.destroy!
      reset_session
      remove_authentication_cookie
    end

    def authenticated_as(session)
      Current.session = session
      set_authentication_cookie(session)
    end

    def post_authenticating_url
      session.delete(:return_to_after_authenticating) || root_url
    end

    def set_authentication_cookie(session)
      cookies.signed.permanent[:session_token] = { value: session.token, httponly: true, same_site: :lax }
    end

    def remove_authentication_cookie
      cookies.delete(:session_token)
    end
end

class Rooms::OpensController < RoomsController
  before_action :set_room, only: %i[ show edit update ]
  before_action :ensure_can_administer, only: %i[ update ]
  before_action :remember_last_room_visited, only: :show
  before_action :force_room_type, only: %i[ edit update ]
  before_action :ensure_permission_to_create_rooms, only: %i[ new create ]

  DEFAULT_ROOM_NAME = "New room"

  def show
    redirect_to room_url(@room)
  end

  def new
    @room = Rooms::Open.new(name: DEFAULT_ROOM_NAME)
    @users = User.active.ordered
  end

  def create
    room = Rooms::Open.create_for(room_params, users: Current.user)

    broadcast_create_room(room)
    redirect_to room_url(room)
  end

  def edit
    @users = User.active.ordered
  end

  def update
    @room.update! room_params

    broadcast_update_room
    redirect_to room_url(@room)
  end

  private
    # Allows us to edit a closed room and turn it into an open one on saving.
    def force_room_type
      @room = @room.becomes!(Rooms::Open)
    end

    # Open and closed rooms convert into each other, so both are in reach here. Direct
    # rooms never are: promoting one would republish its history to the whole account.
    def room_scope
      Current.user.rooms.without_directs
    end

    def broadcast_create_room(room)
      broadcast_prepend_to :rooms, target: :shared_rooms, partial: "users/sidebars/rooms/shared", locals: { room: room }
    end

    def broadcast_update_room
      broadcast_replace_to :rooms, target: [ @room, :list ], partial: "users/sidebars/rooms/shared", locals: { room: @room }
    end
end

class Rooms::InvolvementsController < ApplicationController
  include RoomScoped

  def show

    @membership.update! involvement: params[:involvement]

class Users::AvatarsController < ApplicationController
  include ActiveStorage::Streaming

  rescue_from(ActiveSupport::MessageVerifier::InvalidSignature) { head :not_found }

  def show
    @user = User.from_avatar_token(params[:user_id])

    if stale?(etag: @user)

      if (avatar_variant = @user.avatar_variant)
        send_webp_blob_file avatar_variant.key
      else
        render_initials
      end
    end

    redirect_to user_profile_url

      send_file ActiveStorage::Blob.service.path_for(key), content_type: "image/webp", disposition: :inline
    end

    def render_initials
      render formats: :svg
    end

**Security Deep Dive: Bot Authentication and Code Management**

Alright, let's break this down systematically. I need to make sure this bot code is rock solid. First, I’m seeing some similarities between the transfer and invite links in `_transfer.html.erb` and `_invite.html.erb`, which is interesting, but my focus is the bot code itself.

The prompt emphasizes that "The bot code is a sensitive credential". So, every facet of its security needs examination. Here's what I'm thinking:

1.  **Generation:** I need high entropy. Something like `SecureRandom.base58(24)` or `SecureRandom.alphanumeric(24)` is the right direction—around 140 bits of entropy is great; it's short, clean, and not prone to leaks in URLs like base64. It’s significantly stronger than the original Campfire's use of 12 characters.

    *   I need to avoid storing only a digest because the prompt says the code *must* be displayed in the UI, and if it's displayed, it *cannot* be a one-way hash.
2.  **Comparison:** Constant-time comparison is crucial. `ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare` is the way to go here. It’ll prevent timing attacks.
3.  **Uniqueness:** Every bot needs a unique code. I'll enforce this with a database unique index. If a collision *does* happen, a regeneration mechanism is required.
4.  **Scoping/Authorization:** This is where things get interesting.
    *   I need to limit who can see and manage the bots. The creator and admins should have full access, while normal users are restricted to their bots.
    *   The bot code *cannot* be exposed anywhere public, in URLs, in API responses, in HTML attributes, etc. That's a huge vulnerability.
    *   Cache control is key. I'll apply `Cache-Control: no-store` to the `/bots` endpoint. This prevents caching of bot credentials in browsers, proxies, and Turbo Drive’s cache, protecting bot secrets. I need to check if this impacts tests or navigation.

5.  **Logging & Parameter Filtering:** I will filter `:bot_key`, `:bot_token`, and `:bot_code` in the parameter logging. The fact that Rails applies `config.filter_parameters` to `ActiveRecord#inspect` is a good built-in feature, to ensure the credentials are automatically masked from `bot.inspect`.
6.  **Authentication Order and Error Handling:** The prompt mentions the HTTP status codes. The authentication *must* be done before checking room ID or access. So, a `401 Unauthorized` should always be returned if the bot code is invalid, *even* if a room ID is bad. This prevents an attacker from probing valid room IDs.

    *   I'll carefully ensure the bot cannot post to rooms that it's not a member of. I'll use a `RoomScoped` concern to handle this. Bots can only post to rooms they have membership in.
    *   If a room is deleted or the bot is removed from a room, access is immediately revoked, resulting in a `404 Not Found`. I'll need to think about how to handle bot deletion.
7.  **Rate Limiting:** I'm cautious about rate limiting bot requests. QA and CI tests might send a lot of requests. I'll need to implement rate limiting very carefully, if at all. Invalid code attempts are different—I'll need to weigh the risk of brute-force attacks against any potential disruption to testing. I need to review the testing environment and potentially the rate limiting configurations in `config/environments/`.
8.  **Preventing Web Login:** A bot should *never* be able to log in via a web session. I'll need to check the `users` table schema, particularly `email_address` and `password_digest`. The schema shows the email is nullable, but a unique index will allow multiple `null` values. I must ensure the authentication logic, such as `SessionsController`, specifically excludes bot logins. I'll scope sessions to `User.active.not_bot` (or `User.active.where.not(role: :bot)`). Further, I'll need to review the `password_digest` and consider whether it is safe to set to null for bots. Finally, I will check the original migration that makes `password_digest` non-nullable, to understand why.

**Analyzing Controller Concerns for Bot API Access**

And then, back to `AllowBrowser`: it defines versions for different browsers. Interesting. So, what happens if I send a request to a subclass of `ApplicationController` using something like `curl`?

`allow_browser` checks the User-Agent string. With a standard `curl` request (e.g., `curl/8.x`), `allow_browser` probably allows the request by default, which is good. Rails' `allow_browser` only blocks recognized *older* versions of safari/chrome/firefox/opera/ie.

Now, hold on. What about `protect_from_forgery with: :exception` in `Authentication`? That's going to be a problem. If I send a `curl -d "..." https://.../rooms/<room-id>/<bot-code>/messages` request, I'm going to get a `422 InvalidAuthenticityToken` unless I explicitly *skip* CSRF verification. And I need to skip it specifically for that bot endpoint. Remember that in `test.rb`, `allow_forgery_protection = false`, so you wouldn't even notice this in tests unless you explicitly test or remember `skip_forgery_protection` (or `protect_from_forgery except: ...` or `skip_before_action :verify_authenticity_token`)! That's a critical catch!

Alright, let's focus on the bot message posting controller (`Messages::ByBotsController`). It needs to *allow unauthenticated access* (or skip `require_authentication`) – I'll authenticate via the bot code instead! And I absolutely *must* `skip_forgery_protection` since the bots are posting via `curl` and don't provide CSRF tokens, using the bot code credential.

Next, what about `BlockBannedRequests`? It blocks banned IPs on non-safe requests. That's fine; it doesn't cause a problem unless an IP is banned, which is a desirable behavior.

And then, `AllowBrowser`. Even if a bot uses a weird User-Agent (maybe an old IE or some odd CI script), I can probably just `skip_before_action :allow_browser` (or check what callback `allow_browser` installs, or simply inherit from `ActionController::API` or skip `allow_browser`? Wait: let's check if we need view rendering/Turbo broadcasts!). I think the bot endpoint is an API, but it might broadcast using Turbo or have ActiveStorage attachments! Let's check `Messages::ByBotsController`. And, yes! `Messages::ByBotsController` calls `@message.broadcast_create`, which uses `Turbo::Streams::Broadcasts` from the model (`Message::Broadcasts`), and `ActiveStorage::SetCurrent` might be needed if attachments are processed/broadcast!

Let's check `MessagesController`. Okay, it includes `ActiveStorage::SetCurrent`. That's important! It sets `ActiveStorage::Current.url_options` (from `request`), so any URLs generated during attachment processing or broadcasting will have the right host/protocol. Plus, `ApplicationController` includes `SetCurrentRequest` which sets `Current.request = request` and `default_url_options`!

Finally, I need to check how `allow_browser` is *actually* working in Rails 8.1. I need to make sure `curl` and arbitrary User-Agents are still allowed or if I need to skip it on the bot API endpoint. I'll need to inspect it via `rails runner`.

Scoping `SessionsController#create` and `Sessions::TransfersController#update` to `User.active.without_bots` ensures bots *never* authenticate as web sessions or transfers. This avoids unintended security risks.

Next, we must thoroughly vet every place in the codebase that queries `User` to properly include or exclude bots.

require "test_helper"

class MessagesControllerTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  setup do
    host! "once.campfire.test"

    sign_in :david
    @room = rooms(:watercooler)
    @messages = @room.messages.ordered.to_a
  end

  test "index returns the last page by default" do
    get room_messages_url(@room)

    assert_response :success
    ensure_messages_present @messages.last
  end

  test "index returns a page before the specified message" do
    get room_messages_url(@room, before: @messages.third)

    assert_response :success
    ensure_messages_present @messages.first, @messages.second
    ensure_messages_not_present @messages.third, @messages.fourth, @messages.fifth
  end

  test "index returns a page after the specified message" do
    get room_messages_url(@room, after: @messages.third)

    assert_response :success
    ensure_messages_present @messages.fourth, @messages.fifth
    ensure_messages_not_present @messages.first, @messages.second, @messages.third
  end

  test "index returns no_content when there are no messages" do
    @room.messages.destroy_all

    get room_messages_url(@room)

    assert_response :no_content
  end

  test "get renders a single message belonging to the user" do
    message = @room.messages.where(creator: users(:david)).first

    get room_message_url(@room, message)

    assert_response :success
  end

  test "creating a message broadcasts the message to the room" do
    post room_messages_url(@room, format: :turbo_stream), params: { message: { body: "New one", client_message_id: 999 } }

    assert_rendered_turbo_stream_broadcast @room, :messages, action: "append", target: [ @room, :messages ] do
      assert_select ".message__body", text: /New one/
      assert_copy_link_button room_at_message_url(@room, Message.last, host: "once.campfire.test")
    end
  end

  test "creating a message broadcasts unread room to each member" do
    @room.users.each do |member|
      assert_broadcasts UnreadRoomsChannel.stream_name_for(member.id), 1 do
        post room_messages_url(@room, format: :turbo_stream), params: { message: { body: "New one #{member.id}", client_message_id: member.id } }
      end
    end
  end

  test "creating a message doesn't broadcast unread room to non-members" do
    outsiders = User.where.not(id: @room.users.map(&:id))
    assert outsiders.any?, "need someone outside the room for this test to mean anything"

    outsiders.each do |outsider|
      assert_no_broadcasts UnreadRoomsChannel.stream_name_for(outsider.id) do
        post room_messages_url(@room, format: :turbo_stream), params: { message: { body: "New one", client_message_id: 999 } }
      end
    end
  end

  test "update updates a message belonging to the user" do
    message = @room.messages.where(creator: users(:david)).first

    Turbo::StreamsChannel.expects(:broadcast_replace_to).once
    put room_message_url(@room, message), params: { message: { body: "Updated body" } }

    assert_redirected_to room_message_url(@room, message)
    assert_equal "Updated body", message.reload.plain_text_body
  end

  test "admin updates a message belonging to another user" do
    message = @room.messages.where(creator: users(:jason)).first

    Turbo::StreamsChannel.expects(:broadcast_replace_to).once
    put room_message_url(@room, message), params: { message: { body: "Updated body" } }

    assert_redirected_to room_message_url(@room, message)
    assert_equal "Updated body", message.reload.plain_text_body
  end

  test "destroy destroys a message belonging to the user" do
    message = @room.messages.where(creator: users(:david)).first

    assert_difference -> { Message.count }, -1 do
      Turbo::StreamsChannel.expects(:broadcast_remove_to).once
      delete room_message_url(@room, message, format: :turbo_stream)
      assert_response :success
    end
  end

  test "admin destroy destroys a message belonging to another user" do

      }, &
  rescue Exception => e
    Sentry.capture_exception(e, extra: { message: message })
    Rails.logger.error "Exception while rendering message #{message.class.name}##{message.id}, failed with: #{e.class} `#{e.message}`"

    render "messages/unrenderable"
  end

  def message_timestamp(message, **attributes)
    local_datetime_tag message.created_at, **attributes
  end

    case message.content_type
    when "attachment"
      message_attachment_presentation(message)
    when "sound"
      message_sound_presentation(message)

      auto_link h(ContentFilters::TextMessagePresentationFilters.apply(message.body.body)), html: { target: "_blank" }
    end

    Rails.logger.error "Exception while generating message representation for #{message.class.name}##{message.id}, failed with: #{e.class} `#{e.message}`"

    ""
  end

messages.thinking: **Analyzing Message Body Rendering** Okay, let's dive into the guts of how message bodies are handled, specifically looking at `MessagesHelperTest` and `ContentFilters`. My initial observation is focused on what happens when a `message.body` is rendered. I see that the `body` is actually an ActionText RichText field, using `has_rich_text :body`. The rendering process is where the interesting stuff happens. I notice that `ContentFilters::TextMessagePresentationFilters` get executed. Within this filter chain, I see a few key transformations occurring. First, `RemoveSoloUnfurledLinkText` seems to be responsible for removing those pesky solo unfurled link texts. Okay, so I've just had a major breakthrough in how we're going to process bot messages, and I need to document it meticulously. We're dealing with character encodings, content types, and how we're handling attachments in our Rails application. First of all, the `ASCII-8BIT` encoding was a red flag! When a `curl -d` with a UTF-8 character (like the checkmark, ✅) gets mangled, it's a disaster waiting to happen. Thankfully, we have the `request.raw_post` which is crucial. By using `.force_encoding(Encoding::UTF_8)` and `.scrub`, we can handle any character set and ensure proper rendering.

We had to carefully consider the content types. If a user posts using `curl -d`, the `Content-Type` will be `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`. The important thing here is to recognize that we *aren't* URL-decoding the raw post. If the raw request body is `"2 + 2 = 4"`, then *that* is the message! Not `"2 + 2 = 4"`. This means we are maintaining the exact string. If `+` gets URL-encoded into a space, that's a problem.

Then came the attachment handling. If `params[:attachment]` is present, it *could* be an attachment, but we need to verify it is an actual uploaded file (and not just a string sent via `curl -d`). If the `Content-Type` is `multipart/form-data`, then it should be an attachment; otherwise, we handle the raw body. Crucially, we have to check with `.is_a?(ActionDispatch::Http::UploadedFile)` and look for `request.content_mime_type&.== :multipart_form` or if it's got a `.tempfile` – which handles cases where a bot sends `curl -F "attachment=hello"` and prevents ActiveStorage from crashing! If `params[:attachment]` is an uploaded file, we create an attachment message. If not (and if the request *is* multipart!), then it's `422 Unprocessable Content`.

Finally, and this is critical, we checked the HTTP response codes, and the `Location` header, to be exactly what the prompt specifies. The use of relative paths in the location header is essential.

messages.thinking:
**Bot API Security Review**

Okay, let's break this down systematically. My primary concern here is the security of this bot API, specifically in how it handles user-provided data, and I'm leveraging my Campfire expertise to compare and contrast.

It appears the `Message` model in Campfire leverages `has_rich_text :body`, and crucially, the `ContentFilters::TextMessagePresentationFilters` filter stack. This already provides safe HTML sanitization via `SanitizeTags` and `SanitizeAttributes`. So, sending `raw_body` directly to the `message.body` should be safe, and mirror's Campfire's own bot API design philosophy. This allows for plain text, safe HTML formatting, and, critically, neutralizes XSS vectors. The `auto_link` feature is a bonus for handling URLs. Even an empty or HTML-only raw body is rendered safely as empty. The integration with sound commands, like `/play trombone`, looks clean because of the checks on the text body. The UTF-8 encoding fix is good defensive coding.

I wanted to double-check the interaction of `create_with_attachment!` and message creation, and I examined the logic in `Message/attachment.rb` and the corresponding `MessagesController#create` method. The attachment handling is well-defined, correctly analyzes attachments and builds thumbnails when present. The no-attachment case is gracefully handled, with the `ensure_attachment_analyzed` being a no-op when no attachment is passed, and also handles a case with an image attachment.

Now, the critical edge cases. I needed to carefully review how `params[:attachment]` and `request.raw_post` are handled, especially when sending an attachment via `curl -F "attachment=@earth.png"`.

I’ve followed the control flow within `MessagesController#create`, examining the use of `attachment_uploaded?` and `raw_text_body` helper methods. I've traced through a variety of scenarios:

1.  Standard text message: handled correctly.
2.  "text/plain" content type with body: Correct.
3.  Non-file `attachment` value: Handled as text.
4.  Valid file upload (multipart): processed correctly.
5.  Empty message or no data: Returns `422 Unprocessable Content`.
6.  Empty data with content: Correct.
7.  "   " with content: Correct.
8.  Multipart with no attachment: Returns `422`.

And then, I realized the potential vulnerability with `application/json` or `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` data. If a CI script sends potentially malformed data or a request body using invalid JSON, or invalid URL encoded body, what happens when it's accessed via `params`? module User::Bot
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    belongs_to :creator, class_name: "User", optional: true

    before_validation :initialize_bot, on: :create, if: :bot?

    scope :without_bots, -> { where.not(role: :bot) }
  end

  class_methods do
    def create_bot!(attributes)
      create! attributes.merge(role: :bot)
    end

    def authenticate_bot(bot_key)
      id, token = bot_key.to_s.split("-", 2)
      return nil unless id&.match?(/\A\d+\z/) && token.present?

      if bot = active.bot.find_by(id: id)
        bot if bot.bot_token.present? && ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare(bot.bot_token, token)
      end
    end
  end

  def bot_key
    "#{id}-#{bot_token}" if bot? && bot_token.present?
  end

  private
    def initialize_bot
      self.bot_token ||= generate_bot_token
      self.password_digest ||= ""
    end

    def generate_bot_token
      SecureRandom.base58(24)
    end
end
EOF

class Messages::ByBotsController < ApplicationController
  include ActiveStorage::SetCurrent

  allow_unauthenticated_access
  skip_forgery_protection

  before_action :authenticate_bot, :set_room

  def set_request!(request)
    unless request.media_type == "multipart/form-data"
      request.set_header("action_dispatch.request.request_parameters", {})
    end
    super
  end

  def create
    if attachment_uploaded?
      @message = @room.messages.create_with_attachment!(attachment: params[:attachment], creator: @bot)
    elsif (body = raw_text_body).present?
      @message = @room.messages.create!(body: body, creator: @bot)
    else
      return head :unprocessable_content
    end

    @message.broadcast_create
    head :created, location: message_path(@message)
  end

  private
    def allow_browser(*)
    end

    def authenticate_bot
      if @bot = User.authenticate_bot(params[:bot_key])
        Current.user = @bot
      else
        head :unauthorized
      end
    end

    def set_room
      if params[:room_id].to_s.match?(/\A\d+\z/)
        @room = @bot.rooms.find_by(id: params[:room_id])
      end

      head :not_found unless @room
    end

    def attachment_uploaded?
      request.media_type == "multipart/form-data" &&
        params[:attachment].is_a?(ActionDispatch::Http::UploadedFile)
    end

    def raw_text_body
      return if request.media_type == "multipart/form-data"

      body = request.raw_post.dup.force_encoding(Encoding::UTF_8)
      body.valid_encoding? ? body : body.scrub
    end
end
EOF

require "test_helper"

class User::BotTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  test "creating a bot sets role, generates unique bot_token and bot_key, and joins all open rooms" do
    bot = nil
    assert_difference -> { Membership.count }, +Rooms::Open.count do
      bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: users(:kevin))
    end

    assert bot.bot?
    assert bot.active?
    assert_equal users(:kevin), bot.creator
    assert_equal "", bot.password_digest
    assert_nil bot.email_address
    assert_match /\A[A-Za-z0-9]{24}\z/, bot.bot_token
    assert_equal "#{bot.id}-#{bot.bot_token}", bot.bot_key
    assert_equal Rooms::Open.pluck(:id).sort, bot.rooms.pluck(:id).sort

    other_bot = User.create_bot!(name: "CI Bot", creator: users(:kevin))
    assert_not_equal bot.bot_token, other_bot.bot_token
    assert_not_equal bot.bot_key, other_bot.bot_key
  end

  test "bot name is required" do
    bot = User.new(role: :bot, name: "   ", creator: users(:kevin))
    assert_not bot.valid?
    assert_includes bot.errors[:name], "can't be blank"
  end

  test "authenticate_bot validates bot_key strictly" do
    bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: users(:kevin))

    assert_equal bot, User.authenticate_bot(bot.bot_key)

    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot(nil)
    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot("")
    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot("invalid")
    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot("#{bot.id}-wrongtoken")
    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot("#{bot.id}abc-#{bot.bot_token}")
    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot("999999-#{bot.bot_token}")
    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot("#{bot.id}-#{bot.bot_token}-extra")
    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot("#{users(:david).id}-#{bot.bot_token}")
  end

  test "deactivating a bot revokes its token, removes non-direct memberships, preserves messages, and blocks authentication" do
    bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: users(:kevin))
    old_key = bot.bot_key
    message = rooms(:hq).messages.create!(body: "Deploy done", creator: bot)

    bot.deactivate
    bot.reload

    assert bot.deactivated?
    assert_nil bot.bot_token
    assert_nil bot.bot_key
    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot(old_key)
    assert_empty bot.memberships.without_direct_rooms
    assert Message.exists?(message.id)
    assert_equal bot, message.reload.creator
  end

  test "creating a new open room grants membership to active bots but not deactivated bots" do
    active_bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Active Bot", creator: users(:kevin))
    deleted_bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Deleted Bot", creator: users(:kevin))
    deleted_bot.deactivate

    room = Rooms::Open.create_for({ name: "Releases", creator: users(:david) }, users: users(:david))

    assert_includes room.reload.users, active_bot
    assert_not_includes room.users, deleted_bot
  end

  test "can_administer? allows creator and administrators but denies other members" do
    bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: users(:kevin))

    assert users(:kevin).can_administer?(bot)
    assert users(:david).can_administer?(bot)
    assert_not users(:jz).can_administer?(bot)
    assert_not bot.can_administer?
    assert_not bot.can_administer?(rooms(:hq))
  end

  test "bot_token is filtered in inspect output" do
    bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: users(:kevin))

    assert_not_includes bot.inspect, bot.bot_token
    assert_includes bot.inspect, "[FILTERED]"
  end
end

require "test_helper"

class Messages::ByBotsControllerTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  setup do
    host! "once.campfire.test"
    @bot = User.create_bot!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: users(:kevin))
    @open_room = rooms(:hq)
    @closed_room = rooms(:watercooler)
  end

  test "posting raw text with curl default content type creates message and returns 201 with Location header" do
    body = "Deploy of v1.2.3 finished ✅"

    assert_difference -> { @open_room.messages.count }, +1 do
      post room_bot_messages_url(@open_room, @bot.bot_key),
        params: body,
        headers: { "Content-Type" => "application/x-www-form-urlencoded", "User-Agent" => "curl/8.5.0" }
    end

    message = @open_room.messages.order(:id).last
    assert_response :created
    assert_equal "/messages/#{message.id}", response.headers["Location"]
    assert_equal @bot, message.creator
    assert_equal body, message.plain_text_body
  end

  test "posting raw text with special characters (%, &, =, brackets) does not fail form parsing" do
    [
      "Deploy 100% complete!",
      "foo=1&foo[bar]=2",
      "Build [main] finished: 2 + 2 = 4",
      '{"raw": "json without envelope"}'
    ].each do |raw_text|
      post room_bot_messages_url(@open_room, @bot.bot_key),
        params: raw_text,
        headers: { "Content-Type" => "application/x-www-form-urlencoded" }

      assert_response :created, "Failed for body: #{raw_text.inspect}"
      assert_equal raw_text, @open_room.messages.order(:id).last.plain_text_body
    end
  end

  test "posting raw text with text/plain content type succeeds" do
    post room_bot_messages_url(@open_room, @bot.bot_key),
      params: "Plain text alert",
      headers: { "Content-Type" => "text/plain; charset=utf-8" }

    assert_response :created
    assert_equal "Plain text alert", @open_room.messages.order(:id).last.plain_text_body
  end

  test "bot message renders with bot name as author in room view" do
    post room_bot_messages_url(@open_room, @bot.bot_key),
      params: "Deploy of v1.2.3 finished ✅",
      headers: { "Content-Type" => "application/x-www-form-urlencoded" }

    assert_response :created

    sign_in :david
    get room_url(@open_room)
    assert_response :ok

    message = @open_room.messages.order(:id).last
    assert_select "##{dom_id(message)}" do
      assert_select ".message__author strong", text: "Deploy Bot"
      assert_select ".message__body", text: /Deploy of v1\.2\.3 finished ✅/
    end
  end

  test "bot message broadcasts to connected clients and notifies room members only" do
    post room_bot_messages_url(@open_room, @bot.bot_key),
      params: "Live deploy broadcast",
      headers: { "Content-Type" => "application/x-www-form-urlencoded" }

    assert_response :created
    assert_rendered_turbo_stream_broadcast @open_room, :messages, action: "append", target: [ @open_room, :messages ] do
      assert_select ".message__author strong", text: "Deploy Bot"
      assert_select ".message__body", text: /Live deploy broadcast/
    end

    @closed_room.memberships.grant_to(@bot)
    @closed_room.users.each do |member|
      assert_broadcasts UnreadRoomsChannel.stream_name_for(member.id), 1 do
        post room_bot_messages_url(@closed_room, @bot.bot_key),
          params: "Ping #{member.id}",
          headers: { "Content-Type" => "application/x-www-form-urlencoded" }
      end
    end

    outsiders = User.where.not(id: @closed_room.user_ids)
    assert outsiders.any?
    outsiders.each do |outsider|
      assert_no_broadcasts UnreadRoomsChannel.stream_name_for(outsider.id) do
        post room_bot_messages_url(@closed_room, @bot.bot_key),
          params: "Private room message",
          headers: { "Content-Type" => "application/x-www-form-urlencoded" }
      end
    end
  end

  test "bot message triggers web push notifications with bot name as author" do
    expected_subscriptions = Push::Subscription
      .joins(user: :memberships)
      .merge(Membership.visible.disconnected.involved_in_everything.where(room: @open_room).where.not(user: @bot))
    expected_count = expected_subscriptions.count
    assert expected_count > 0

    assert_enqueued_jobs 1, only: [ Room::PushMessageJob ] do
      post room_bot_messages_url(@open_room, @bot.bot_key),
        params: "Deploy of v1.2.3 finished ✅",
        headers: { "Content-Type" => "application/x-www-form-urlencoded" }
    end
    assert_response :created

    delivered_payloads = []
    WebPush.stubs(:payload_send).with do |args|
      delivered_payloads << JSON.parse(args[:message])
      true
    end

    perform_enqueued_jobs only: Room::PushMessageJob
    wait_for_web_push_delivery_pool_tasks(expected_count)

    assert_equal expected_count, delivered_payloads.size
    delivered_payloads.each do |payload|
      assert_equal @open_room.name, payload["title"]
      assert_equal "Deploy Bot: Deploy of v1.2.3 finished ✅", payload["options"]["body"]
    end
  end

  test "posting an attachment via multipart creates attachment message and returns 201" do
    assert_difference -> { @open_room.messages.count }, +1 do
      assert_enqueued_jobs 1, only: [ Room::PushMessageJob ] do
        post room_bot_messages_url(@open_room, @bot.bot_key),
          params: { attachment: fixture_file_upload("earth.png", "image/png") }
      end
    end

    message = @open_room.messages.order(:id).last
    assert_response :created
    assert_equal "/messages/#{message.id}", response.headers["Location"]
    assert message.attachment.attached?
    assert_equal "earth.png", message.plain_text_body
    assert_equal @bot, message.creator
  end

  test "empty body and no attachment returns 422 Unprocessable Content" do
    assert_no_difference -> { Message.count } do
      post room_bot_messages_url(@open_room, @bot.bot_key)
      assert_response :unprocessable_content

      post room_bot_messages_url(@open_room, @bot.bot_key),
        params: "",
        headers: { "Content-Type" => "application/x-www-form-urlencoded" }
      assert_response :unprocessable_content

      post room_bot_messages_url(@open_room, @bot.bot_key),
        params: "   \n\t  ",
        headers: { "Content-Type" => "text/plain" }
      assert_response :unprocessable_content

      post room_bot_messages_url(@open_room, @bot.bot_key),
        params: { other: "value" },
        headers: { "Content-Type" => "multipart/form-data" }
      assert_response :unprocessable_content
    end
  end

  test "invalid bot code returns 401 Unauthorized even if room id is invalid" do
    [
      "invalid",
      "bad.code",
      "#{@bot.id}-wrongtoken",
      "#{@bot.id}x-#{@bot.bot_token}",
      "#{users(:david).id}-#{@bot.bot_token}",
      "999999-#{@bot.bot_token}"
    ].each do |bad_code|
      post room_bot_messages_url(@open_room, bad_code), params: "Hello"
      assert_response :unauthorized, "Expected 401 for #{bad_code.inspect}"

      post room_bot_messages_url(999999, bad_code), params: "Hello"
      assert_response :unauthorized, "Expected 401 before 404 for #{bad_code.inspect}"
    end
  end

  test "deleted bot returns 401 Unauthorized" do
    old_key = @bot.bot_key
    @bot.deactivate

    assert_no_difference -> { Message.count } do
      post room_bot_messages_url(@open_room, old_key), params: "Hello after delete"
    end
    assert_response :unauthorized
  end

  test "bad room id or room without membership returns 404 Not Found" do
    assert_no_difference -> { Message.count } do
      post room_bot_messages_url(999999, @bot.bot_key), params: "Hello"
      assert_response :not_found

      post room_bot_messages_url("not-a-room", @bot.bot_key), params: "Hello"
      assert_response :not_found

      post room_bot_messages_url("#{@open_room.id}abc", @bot.bot_key), params: "Hello"
      assert_response :not_found

      post room_bot_messages_url(@closed_room, @bot.bot_key), params: "Hello"
      assert_response :not_found
    end
  end

  test "bot can post to closed room after being added and gets 404 after removal" do
    @closed_room.memberships.grant_to(@bot)

    post room_bot_messages_url(@closed_room, @bot.bot_key), params: "Hello closed room"
    assert_response :created
    assert_equal "Hello closed room", @closed_room.messages.order(:id).last.plain_text_body

    @closed_room.memberships.revoke_from(@bot)

    post room_bot_messages_url(@closed_room, @bot.bot_key), params: "After removal"
    assert_response :not_found
  end

  test "bot can post to direct room it belongs to" do
    direct_room = Rooms::Direct.find_or_create_for(User.where(id: [ users(:kevin).id, @bot.id ]))

    post room_bot_messages_url(direct_room, @bot.bot_key), params: "Direct ping"
    assert_response :created
    assert_equal "Direct ping", direct_room.messages.order(:id).last.plain_text_body
  end

  test "endpoint works with CSRF forgery protection enabled and legacy User-Agent" do
    previous_forgery_setting = ActionController::Base.allow_forgery_protection
    ActionController::Base.allow_forgery_protection = true

    post room_bot_messages_url(@open_room, @bot.bot_key),
      params: "From CI with CSRF on",
      headers: {
        "Content-Type" => "application/x-www-form-urlencoded",
        "User-Agent" => "Mozilla/4.0 (compatible; MSIE 6.0; Windows NT 5.1)"
      }

    assert_response :created
    assert_equal "From CI with CSRF on", @open_room.messages.order(:id).last.plain_text_body
  ensure
    ActionController::Base.allow_forgery_protection = previous_forgery_setting
  end

  private
    def wait_for_web_push_delivery_pool_tasks(count)
      pool = Rails.configuration.x.web_push_pool.delivery_pool
      start = Time.now
      timeout = 1.0
      while pool.completed_task_count < count
        raise "Timeout waiting for pool tasks to complete" if Time.now - start > timeout
        sleep 0.01
      end
    end
end

cat <<'EOF' > docs/bots.md
# Bots Design Notes

## Data Model

Bots are modeled as `User` records with `role: :bot` (`enum :role, %i[ member administrator bot ]` in `User::Role`) and bot-specific behavior in `User::Bot`:

- `users.bot_token` (string, unique index): 24-character `SecureRandom.base58(24)` secret (~140 bits of entropy), generated on create via `before_validation :initialize_bot, on: :create, if: :bot?`.
- `users.creator_id` (foreign key to `users`, `on_delete: :nullify`): tracks the user who created the bot so `User#can_administer?` works uniformly for bots (creators manage their own bots; administrators manage all bots).
- `users.password_digest`: initialized to `""` on bot creation (`has_secure_password` returns `false` for all password checks when blank). `email_address` remains `nil`.
- `User#bot_key`: returns `"#{id}-#{bot_token}"` for active bots.

## Authentication & Authorization

- **Bot credential verification (`User.authenticate_bot`)**: splits `bot_key` into `id` and `token`, validates `id` is strictly digits (`/\A\d+\z/`), looks up `User.active.bot.find_by(id: id)`, and verifies `bot_token` with `ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare`.
- **Bot management UI (`/bots`)**:
  - Accessible to all signed-in chat members via `/account/edit` ("Set up chat bots").
  - Members see only active bots they created; administrators see all active bots. Rendered on one page without pagination.
  - `BotsController` sets `Cache-Control: no-store` on `index` and `edit` because bot codes are sensitive credentials.
  - `edit`, `update`, and `destroy` scope to `User.active.bot` (returning `404` for human users or deleted bots) and enforce `Current.user.can_administer?(@bot)` (returning `403` for other members' bots).
- **Deletion**: deleting a bot calls `User#deactivate`, which marks the bot `deactivated`, clears `bot_token` to `nil`, removes non-direct room memberships, and preserves previously posted messages with the bot shown as author. Deactivated bots immediately fail authentication with `401 Unauthorized`.
- **Human-only surfaces**: `AccountsController`, `Accounts::UsersController`, `SessionsController`, `Sessions::TransfersController`, and `Users::BansController` scope to `User.without_bots` so bots cannot log in via web sessions or transfer links, do not appear in the people list on `/account/edit`, cannot be promoted/demoted, and cannot be banned.
- **Log filtering**: `bot_token` and route param `:bot_key` match `:token` and `:_key` in `config/initializers/filter_parameter_logging.rb`, filtering them in logs and `ActiveRecord#inspect`.

## Room Membership

- Creating a bot triggers `User`'s `after_create_commit :grant_membership_to_open_rooms`, automatically joining all `Rooms::Open`.
- Creating/converting an open room grants membership to `User.active` (including active bots).
- Closed room forms (`Rooms::ClosedsController`) and direct room / mention autocomplete (`Autocompletable::UsersController`) use `User.active`, allowing bots to be added to closed and direct rooms the same way as people.

## Bot HTTP API

- Route: `POST /rooms/:room_id/:bot_key/messages` (`Messages::ByBotsController#create`), with segment constraints `{ room_id: /[^\/]+/, bot_key: /[^\/]+/ }` so malformed segments (including dotted strings) still route to the controller for proper `401`/`404` handling.
- Skips web session auth, CSRF verification, and `allow_browser` checks.
- Overrides `set_request!` to short-circuit `request_parameters` parsing for non-multipart requests so `curl -d` bodies with `%`, brackets, `&`, or `=` never trigger Rack form-parsing `400 Bad Request` errors and never leak raw message bodies into parameter logs.
- Decodes raw request body bytes as UTF-8 (`force_encoding(Encoding::UTF_8)` with `.scrub` fallback) so emoji and multibyte text sent by `curl -d` are preserved without mojibake.
- Supports file attachments via `multipart/form-data` (`params[:attachment]` as `ActionDispatch::Http::UploadedFile`).
- Check order and responses:
  1. `401 Unauthorized` — invalid/revoked bot code (checked before room lookup to prevent room enumeration).
  2. `404 Not Found` — invalid room ID or room the bot is not a member of.
  3. `422 Unprocessable Content` — blank raw body and no uploaded attachment.
  4. `201 Created` with `Location: /messages/:message_id` — creates message with bot as creator, triggers `room.receive(message)` (unread state + `Room::PushMessageJob`), and calls `@message.broadcast_create`.
EOF
